```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
#Setup
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggbiplot)
library(factoextra)
library(readstata13)
library(sva) #combat!
library(tidyr)
library(vegan)
library(rstatix) #'get summary stats'
library(viridis) #colours for heatmap
library(ggpubr)

#functions
impute=function(x){
  x[is.na(x)] =min(x, na.rm=TRUE)/2 #convert the NA values to half the minimum from the column, these were 7 initially
  x #display the column
}
```

## Bile Acids Analysis
```{r data preprocessing}
# File not provided
data_bile = readstata13::read.dta13(
  "BileacidsandmetadataOct20v2.dta", encoding = "latin1" ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate( pays = factor( pays
                                , levels = 1:2
                                , labels = c("Madagascar","CAR"))
                 , Analysisround = factor( Analysisround
                                           , levels = c(1,2,3,4) # correct the mistaken '#4' to '#3'
                                           , labels = c(1,2,3,3) ) 
                 , stunted = factor( stunted
                                     , levels= 1:0
                                     , labels = c("stunted","non-stunted") )
                 # , sexe = factor(sexe, labels = c("Male","Female"), levels = c("Masculin","FÃ©minin"))
                 , sibo = (UFCml >= 200000)
                 , age_years = cut( age
                                    , breaks = c(24, 36, 48, 61)
                                    , labels = c("2-3 years","3-4 years","4-5 years")
                                    , include.lowest = TRUE
                                    , right = TRUE
                                    , dig.lab = 5
                                    , ordered_result = TRUE )
                 , dplyr::across( .cols = c("anemie","sibo","haz","haz2")
                                  ,.fns = as.factor )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::filter( !SampleType %in% c("internalcontrol", "" ) & stunted != "" ) %>%
  dplyr::rename( #Country  = pays,
    calpro = calprotectinelevel
    , aat    = alphaantitrypsinlevel
    , anemia = anemie
    , batch  = Analysisround ) %>%
  #-- removing observations not supposed to exist
  dplyr::filter( !((SampleType == "Duodenal" | SampleType == 'Gastric') & stunted == "non-stunted" ))

###_- then turning to lowercase
colnames(data_bile) = colnames(data_bile) %>%
  tolower() %>%
  gsub("sulfate", "sul", . ) %>%
  gsub("dexy", "deoxy", . ) %>%
  gsub("glucuronide","gluc", .)

#- add a category lithoderivatives
lithoderivatives<-unique(colnames(data_bile)[grep( pattern = "litho", colnames(data_bile))])
lithoderivatives_r<-unique(lithoderivatives[grep( pattern = "_r", lithoderivatives)])
data_bile$lithoderivatives_r = rowSums(data_bile[colnames(data_bile) %in% lithoderivatives_r])

#- add a category urso
urso<-unique(colnames(data_bile)[grep( pattern = "urso", colnames(data_bile))])
urso_r<-unique(urso[grep( pattern = "_r", urso)])
data_bile$urso_r = rowSums(data_bile[colnames(data_bile) %in% urso_r])

#-- fixing column capitalization
colnames(data_bile)[ colnames(data_bile) == "sampletype"] = "SampleType"

#--correct the mistaken 'batch 4' to 'batch 3'
data_bile$batch[which(data_bile$batch==4)] <- 3 

#-- metadata columns
meta_cols = colnames(data_bile)[c( 1:833, 999) ]
Meta      = data_bile %>% dplyr::select( all_of( meta_cols ) ) #take metadata only

#-- bile acid columns
bile_cols = colnames(data_bile)[c( 834:998, 1000:1007) ]
bile_acids      = data_bile %>% dplyr::select( all_of( bile_cols ) ) #take bile acid data only

#--- only the relative abundance columns
acids_rel_abund_col = colnames(data_bile)[ grep(pattern = "_r", colnames(data_bile))]
acids_rel_abund_col <- setdiff(acids_rel_abund_col, meta_cols) #remove accidental metadata
acids_rel_abund = data_bile %>% dplyr::select( all_of( bile_cols ) ) #take rel abundance bile acid data only

#--- only the NON relative abundance columns - absolute numbers for revisions as per reviewer #3 Q2
acids_abund_col = colnames(data_bile)[c(834:913, 915:916)] #bad solution for picking columns
acids_abund_col <- setdiff(acids_abund_col, meta_cols) #remove accidental metadata
acids_abund = data_bile %>% dplyr::select( all_of( acids_abund_col ) ) #take rel abundance bile acid data only

#--- only the ratios
acids_ratio_col = colnames(data_bile)[ grep(pattern = "ratio", colnames(data_bile))]
acids_ratio = data_bile %>% dplyr::select( all_of( acids_ratio_col ) ) #take rel abundance bile acid data only

#--- only the grouped as relative abundance
bile_grouped_cols = colnames(data_bile)[c( 990:998, 1006:1007)]
bile_acids_grouped      = data_bile %>% dplyr::select( all_of( bile_grouped_cols ) ) #take bile acid data only

#only the single bile acids, no categories!
single_bile_acids <- setdiff(acids_rel_abund_col, bile_grouped_cols)
single_bile_acids

#--- main tables
X        = data_bile %>% dplyr::select( all_of(c( acids_rel_abund_col, meta_cols ) )) %>%
  group_by(SampleType) %>%
  filter(!duplicated(id)) %>% #for most downstream analyses, remove the technical duplicates
  ungroup()
X_grouped = data_bile %>% dplyr::select( all_of(c( bile_grouped_cols, meta_cols ) ))
X_ratio = data_bile %>% dplyr::select( all_of(c( acids_ratio_col, meta_cols ) ))


X_CAR= dplyr::filter(X, pays == "CAR")
X_Mada= dplyr::filter(X, pays == "Madagascar")

#subsets by sample type
feces  = dplyr::filter(X, SampleType == "Feces")
feces2 = dplyr::filter(feces, haz2!=1) #to compare only NN and MCS

duodenal = dplyr::filter(X, SampleType=="Duodenal")
gastric = dplyr::filter(X, SampleType=="Gastric")

feces_CAR = dplyr::filter(X, (SampleType=="Feces" & pays=="CAR"))
feces2_CAR = dplyr::filter(feces_CAR, haz2!=1) #to compare only NN and MCS
feces_Mada = dplyr::filter(X, (SampleType=="Feces" & pays=="Madagascar"))
feces2_Mada = dplyr::filter(feces_Mada, haz2!=1) #to compare only NN and MCS

duodenal_CAR = dplyr::filter(X, (SampleType=="Duodenal" & pays=="CAR"))
duodenal_Mada = dplyr::filter(X, (SampleType=="Duodenal" & pays=="Madagascar"))
gastric_CAR= dplyr::filter(X, (SampleType=="Gastric" & pays=="CAR"))
gastric_Mada = dplyr::filter(X, (SampleType=="Gastric" & pays=="Madagascar"))

#check sample size by group
length(feces$id)
length(duodenal$id)
length(gastric$id)

#count for flowchart
dplyr::count(feces, pays, stunted)
dplyr::count(duodenal, pays, stunted)
dplyr::count(gastric, pays, stunted)

#are there any samples missing bile acids data entirely? 
bile_acids_nozeroes <- bile_acids
bile_acids[is.na(bile_acids_nozeroes)] <- 0
bile_acids_nozeroes[which(rowSums(bile_acids_nozeroes)==0),] #no they all have something
```

```{r Fig 1A}
##Fig 1 A-C : Differences in Bile Acids by SampleType
#A: PCoA WITHOUT combat correction
#X = all the bile acids from the full data_bile set.
RelAbundsingle<- X %>% dplyr::select(all_of(single_bile_acids)) #take only the single bile acids

#consider NAs to be zero
# now impute the values which are NA or 0
RelAbundsingle[RelAbundsingle<=0] <- NA # first convert all negative or 0 values in NA
RelAbundsingle=data.frame(apply(RelAbundsingle,2,impute)) #and then impute them as half the minimum value (instead of zero)
dim(RelAbundsingle)
RelAbundsingle_log<-log10(RelAbundsingle)
RelAbundsingle_log<-as.data.frame(RelAbundsingle_log) 

#corresponding metadata 
RelAbundsingle.meta <- X %>% dplyr::select(all_of(meta_cols))

amp.pca.raw <- prcomp(RelAbundsingle_log, scale=TRUE)
summary(amp.pca.raw)
amp.pca.raw$x[1]

eig.val <- get_eigenvalue(amp.pca.raw)
eig.val$variance.percent

RelAbundsingle.meta$SampleType <- factor(RelAbundsingle.meta$SampleType, levels=c("Gastric", "Duodenal", "Feces"))

#pdf("plots/1A_PCA_sampletype_precombatlog.pdf", width=6, height=5)

p
```

```{r Fig 1BCD}
#Test for differences by sample type used a repeated wilcoxen with FDR correction.

# All main bile acid caterogies by Sample Type
# First - uncorrected, by check via glm + batch. #Second - on combat corrected dataset itself.
X_grouped$SampleType <- factor(X_grouped$SampleType, levels = c("Gastric", "Duodenal", "Feces"))
X_ratio$SampleType <- factor(X_ratio$SampleType, levels = c("Gastric", "Duodenal", "Feces"))

#Primary bile acids by sample type. Uncorrected values.
one.way <- kruskal.test(primarymain_r ~ SampleType, data = X_grouped)
one.way #highly significant <2e-16 ***

model <- lm(primarymain_r ~ batch + SampleType, data=X_grouped)
summary(model)

p <- ggplot(X_grouped, aes(y=primarymain_r, x=SampleType)) + geom_boxplot(outlier.shape=NA) + geom_jitter(width=0.1, height=0)
p <- p + theme(panel.background = element_blank(), axis.line = element_line(colour = "black"),
               axis.title.y = element_text(margin = margin(r = 10)))
p <- p + xlab("Sample Type") + ylab("Relative abundance (%)") + ggtitle("Primary Bile Acids")
p <- p + annotate('segment', x=1, xend=3, y=105, yend=105)
p <- p + annotate('text', label='***', x=2, y=110)
Figure1C <- p

pdf("../../Figure_panels/Figure1C.pdf", height = 3, width = 3)
Figure1C
dev.off()

source_data_1C <- X_grouped %>% select(primarymain_r, SampleType)

write.csv2(source_data_1C, "../../Source_data/Figure1C.csv")
```

```{r}
#make a heatmap of all the single bile acids by sample type.
#first: summarize the mean value of each bile acid per sample type (?)
to_summarize <- X %>% dplyr::select(all_of(single_bile_acids)) #start again with single
to_summarize[is.na(to_summarize)] <- 0 #0 is 0, no NAs
to_summarize$SampleType <- X$SampleType #add back grouping variable
AverageBySampleType <- to_summarize %>% group_by(SampleType) %>% summarize_all(mean)
AverageBySampleType #nice :) 
AverageBySampleType <- AverageBySampleType %>% pivot_longer(cols=c(2:length(names(AverageBySampleType))),
                                                            names_to="Bile_Acid", values_to="Relative_Abundance")
AverageBySampleType #double nice :) 
AverageBySampleType <- AverageBySampleType[order(AverageBySampleType$Relative_Abundance),]
AverageBySampleType$SampleType <- factor(AverageBySampleType$SampleType, levels=c("Gastric", "Duodenal", "Feces"))
top_bile_acids <- AverageBySampleType %>% filter(Relative_Abundance>=1)
pdata <- AverageBySampleType %>% filter(Bile_Acid %in% top_bile_acids$Bile_Acid)
AverageBySampleType_Gastric <- AverageBySampleType %>% filter(SampleType=="Gastric")
pdata$Bile_Acid <- factor(pdata$Bile_Acid, levels=AverageBySampleType_Gastric$Bile_Acid)

p <- ggplot(pdata, aes(x=SampleType, y=Bile_Acid, fill=log(Relative_Abundance))) + geom_tile(colour='black')
p <- p + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust=1))
p <- p + xlab(NULL) + ylab(NULL)
p <- p + scale_fill_viridis()
#p <- p + scale_fill_gradient2(low="dodgerblue3", mid="lightgreen", high="firebrick2")
p <- p + labs(fill="Log Rel. Abund.") + ggtitle("Major Bile Acids")


#--- REVISED VERSION Fig 1B: same heatmap, with a sidebar annotating primary vs secondary bile acids ---
#Classification below follows standard bile acid biochemistry (Ridlon et al. 2006, J Lipid Res):
#"Primary" = made directly by the host liver from cholesterol (cholic acid, chenodeoxycholic acid,
#and the muricholic acids, plus their glycine/taurine/sulfate/glucuronide conjugates).
#"Secondary" = produced by gut bacteria modifying primary bile acids (7-dehydroxylation, oxidation,
#epimerization - e.g. deoxycholic acid, lithocholic acid, ursodeoxycholic acid, and their
#derivatives/conjugates).
#NOTE: a handful of these calls are genuinely debated in the literature (e.g. dehydrocholic acid,
#the hyocholic-acid family, and lambda-muricholic acid) - please double check this list against
#however primarymain_r/secondarymain_r were originally defined, and edit the vector below if needed.
#redone, Kelsey, based on what is actually in the text of the manuscript & the figure.
bile_acid_class <- c(
  glycocholic_acid_r               = "Primary",
  glycochenodeoxycholic_acid_r     = "Primary",
  glycodeoxycholic_acid_r          = "Secondary",
  taurochenodeoxycholic_acid_r     = "Primary",
  taurocholic_acid_r               = "Primary",
  taurochenodeoxycholic_acid3sul_r = "Primary",
  cholic_acid_r                    = "Primary",
  deoxycholic_acid_r               = "Secondary",
  chenodeoxycholic_acid_r          = "Primary",
  glycolithocholic_acid3sul_r      = "Secondary",
  lithocholic_acid_r               = "Secondary",
  twelveketolithocholic_acid_r     = "Secondary",
  isolithocholic_acid_r            = "Secondary",
  ursocholic_acid_r                = "Secondary",
  ursodeoxycholic_acid_r           = "Secondary",
  apocholic_acid_r                 = "Secondary",
  dehydrolithocholic_acid_r        = "Secondary",
  ursodeoxycholic_acid3sul_r       = "Secondary"
)

#one row per bile acid actually shown in the heatmap, in the same order as the heatmap y-axis
sidebar_data <- pdata %>% dplyr::distinct(Bile_Acid)
sidebar_data$Class <- bile_acid_class[as.character(sidebar_data$Bile_Acid)]
sidebar_data$Class[is.na(sidebar_data$Class)] <- "Unclassified" #safety net if a new bile acid ever shows up
table(sidebar_data$Class, useNA="ifany") #check nothing fell through as Unclassified

p_sidebar <- ggplot(sidebar_data, aes(x=1, y=Bile_Acid, fill=Class)) + geom_tile(colour='black')
p_sidebar <- p_sidebar + scale_fill_manual(values=c(Primary="black", Secondary="grey80", Unclassified="white"), drop=FALSE)
p_sidebar <- p_sidebar + theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), axis.text.y = element_blank(),
                                axis.ticks = element_blank(), panel.background = element_blank(),
                                legend.key.size = unit(0.4,"cm"), legend.text=element_text(size=9),
                                legend.title=element_text(size=10))
p_sidebar <- p_sidebar + xlab(NULL) + ylab(NULL) + labs(fill="Bile Acid Type")

p_combined <- ggarrange(p_sidebar, p, ncol=2, widths=c(0.35, 1), align="h")

figure_1B <- p_combined

pdf("../../Figure_panels/Figure1B.pdf", height = 3, width = 3)
figure_1B
dev.off()

write.csv2(pdata, "../../Source_data/Figure1B.csv")



#and now: test which ones are significantly different by sample type.
#first: do a repeated kruskal-wallis similar to before.
df_kw <- X %>% dplyr::select(all_of(single_bile_acids)) #start again with single bile acids
df_kw[is.na(df_kw)] <- 0 #0 is 0, no NAs

#test each column (apply 2) by sample type
MW.p = apply(df_kw,2,
             function(x) kruskal.test(c(x)~X$SampleType)$p.value)
p.res = data.frame(Bile_Acid=names(df_kw),MW.p)
# Perform multiple comparison correction using a given method of choice
p.res$rel.fdr <- p.adjust(p.res$MW.p, method="fdr")
p.res$bonferroni <- p.adjust(p.res$MW.p, method="bonferroni") 
p.res[order(p.res$bonferroni),]
p.res.hits <- p.res %>% filter(bonferroni<0.05)
dim(p.res.hits)

#and now do that but with linear models so we can adjust for batch.
MW.lm = apply(df_kw,2,
              function(x) summary(lm(c(x)~X$batch + X$SampleType))$coefficients)
MW.lm 
#this technically works but I guess the question is, what do we really want here...
#each column is the list of first the estimate, then std error, then t value, and the last 5 are p-values for X$batch2, X$batch3, X$SampleTypeFeces, X$SampleTypeGastric
#for example, for the first bile acid:
summary(lm(df_kw$allocholic_acid3sul_r~X$batch + X$SampleType))$coefficients
#taking [4,4] gets us the p-value for feces vs duodenum
summary(lm(df_kw$allocholic_acid3sul_r~X$batch + X$SampleType))$coefficients[4,4]
```

```{r Fig S3 repeated testing by country}
##perform repeated wilcoxen by country within sample type. (combat-adjusted data.)
#feces
MW.p.feces.adj = apply(df_feces,2,
                 function(x) wilcox.test(c(x)~bile_combat_output_F_meta$pays)$p.value)

                 function(x) wilcox.test(c(x)~bile_combat_output_F_meta$pays)$statistic) #add for revisions
p.res.adj.f = data.frame(Bile_Acid=names(MW.p.feces.adj),
                         pval=MW.p.feces.adj,
                         coef=MW.p.feces.res,
                         SampleType=c("Feces"),
                         Test=c("Wilcoxon_combat"),
                         Outcome=c("Country"))
# Perform multiple comparison correction using a given method of choice

p.res.adj.f.hits <- p.res.adj.f %>% filter(qval<0.05)
```

```{r Fig S3 repeated testing by country: nonparametric no ComBat}

#repeat nonparametric testing on the non-ComBat-corrected data. 
##perform repeated wilcoxen by country within sample type. 
#NB: the "LM" dataframe is just the non corrected one. Log adjusted. Rel abund.
#feces
MW.p.feces.adj = apply(df_fecesLM,2,
                 function(x) wilcox.test(c(x)~bile_combat_output_F_meta$pays)$p.value)
MW.p.feces.res = apply(df_fecesLM,2,
                 function(x) wilcox.test(c(x)~bile_combat_output_F_meta$pays)$statistic) #add for revisions
p.res.noc.f = data.frame(Bile_Acid=names(MW.p.feces.adj),
                         pval=MW.p.feces.adj,
                         coef=MW.p.feces.res,
                         SampleType=c("Feces"),
                         Test=c("Wilcoxon"),
                         Outcome=c("Country"))
# Perform multiple comparison correction using a given method of choice
p.res.noc.f$qval <- p.adjust(p.res.noc.f$pval, method="fdr")
p.res.noc.f.hits <- p.res.noc.f %>% filter(qval<0.05)
p.res.noc.f.hits
dim(p.res.noc.f.hits)

#duodenum
MW.p.duo.adj = apply(df_duoLM,2,
                       function(x) wilcox.test(c(x)~bile_combat_output_D_meta$pays)$p.value)
MW.p.duo.res = apply(df_duoLM,2,
                 function(x) wilcox.test(c(x)~bile_combat_output_D_meta$pays)$statistic) #add for revisions
p.res.noc.d = data.frame(Bile_Acid=names(MW.p.duo.adj),
                         pval=MW.p.duo.adj,
                         coef=MW.p.duo.res,
                         SampleType=c("Duodenal"),
                         Test=c("Wilcoxon"),
                          Outcome=c("Country"))
# Perform multiple comparison correction using a given method of choice
p.res.noc.d$qval <- p.adjust(p.res.noc.d$pval, method="fdr")
p.res.noc.d.hits <- p.res.noc.d %>% filter(qval<0.05)
p.res.noc.d.hits
dim(p.res.noc.d.hits)

#gastric
MW.p.gas.adj = apply(df_gasLM,2,
                     function(x) wilcox.test(c(x)~bile_combat_output_G_meta$pays)$p.value)
MW.p.gas.res = apply(df_gasLM,2,
                 function(x) wilcox.test(c(x)~bile_combat_output_G_meta$pays)$statistic) #add for revisions
p.res.noc.g = data.frame(Bile_Acid=names(MW.p.gas.adj),
                         pval=MW.p.gas.adj,
                         coef=MW.p.gas.res,
                         SampleType=c("Gastric"),

                          Outcome=c("Country"))
# Perform multiple comparison correction using a given method of choice
p.res.noc.g$qval <- p.adjust(p.res.noc.g$pval, method="fdr")
p.res.noc.g.hits <- p.res.noc.g %>% filter(qval<0.05)
p.res.noc.g.hits
dim(p.res.noc.g.hits)

#combine, export.
```

```{r Fig S3F diff by country heatmap REVISED}
#make a heatmap of all the single bile acids by sample type.
#revised version: select sig hits based on non-parametric, NON COMBAT CORRECTED data
#NB: this is the actual final Fig S3F
#first: summarize the mean value of each bile acid per sample type AND country (?)
p.res.noc.f.hits #make sure these are correctly from the non combat ones (test=Wilcoxon)
to_summarize <- X %>%
  dplyr::select(all_of(c(p.res.noc.f.hits$Bile_Acid,
                         p.res.adj.f.hits$Bile_Acid,
                         feces_hits_country,
                         "SampleType", "pays")))
to_summarize[is.na(to_summarize)] <- 0 #0 is 0, no NAs
AverageByCountry <- to_summarize %>% group_by(SampleType, pays) %>% summarize_all(mean)
AverageByCountry #nice :) 
AverageByCountry <- AverageByCountry %>% pivot_longer(cols=c(3:length(names(AverageByCountry))),
                                                            names_to="Bile_Acid", values_to="Relative_Abundance")
AverageByCountry #double nice :) 
AverageByCountry <- AverageByCountry[order(AverageByCountry$Relative_Abundance),]
AverageByCountry$SampleType <- factor(AverageByCountry$SampleType, levels=c("Gastric", "Duodenal", "Feces"))

pdata <- AverageByCountry 
mylevels <- AverageByCountry %>% filter(SampleType=="Feces"&pays=="CAR")
pdata$Bile_Acid <- factor(pdata$Bile_Acid, levels=mylevels$Bile_Acid)

#I think maybe better to plot feces only, right? #but also: only if it is significant WITH and WITHOUT combat
pdata <- pdata %>% filter(SampleType=="Feces" & Bile_Acid %in% c(p.res.noc.f.hits$Bile_Acid) 
                          & Bile_Acid %in% c(p.res.adj.f.hits$Bile_Acid))

#scale everything rowwise relative to the average abundance of the bile acid
pdata2 <- pdata %>% group_by(Bile_Acid) %>% mutate(Abund_Avg=mean(Relative_Abundance, na.omit=TRUE))
pdata2$Scaled_Abund <- pdata2$Relative_Abundance / pdata2$Abund_Avg
#add a star in case it is also raw significant in the LMs (with adjustment)
lm_stars <- diff_country %>% filter(SampleType=="Feces"&pval<0.05&Test=="LM_covariates")
pdata2$lm_sig <- ifelse(pdata2$pays=="CAR" & #only put the star for one tile
                          pdata2$Bile_Acid %in% lm_stars$Bile_Acid, "*", "")

p <- ggplot(pdata2, aes(x=pays, y=Bile_Acid, fill=log(Scaled_Abund), label=lm_sig)) + geom_tile(colour='black')
p <- p + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust=1)) + 
  geom_text(colour='white') +
  xlab(NULL) + 
  ylab(NULL) + 
  scale_fill_viridis() + 
  labs(fill="Log Rel. Abund.") + ggtitle("Fecal Bile Acids Differentially Abundant by Country") +
  coord_flip()
FigureS3F <- p

pdf("../../Figure_panels/FigureS3F.pdf")
FigureS3F
dev.off()

write.csv2(pdata2, "../../Source_data/FigureS3F.csv")


#also add a panel for primary vs. secondary bile acids as per Fig 1.
#bile acids defined above.

#one row per bile acid actually shown in the heatmap, in the same order as the heatmap y-axis
sidebar_data <- pdata %>% dplyr::distinct(Bile_Acid)
sidebar_data$Class <- bile_acid_class[as.character(sidebar_data$Bile_Acid)]
sidebar_data$Class[is.na(sidebar_data$Class)] <- "Unclassified" #safety net if a new bile acid ever shows up
table(sidebar_data$Class, useNA="ifany") #check nothing fell through as Unclassified

p_sidebar <- ggplot(sidebar_data, aes(y=1, x=Bile_Acid, fill=Class)) + geom_tile(colour='black')
p_sidebar <- p_sidebar + scale_fill_manual(values=c(Primary="black", Secondary="grey80", Group="white", Unclassified="red"), drop=FALSE)
p_sidebar <- p_sidebar + theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), axis.text.y = element_blank(),
                                axis.ticks = element_blank(), panel.background = element_blank(),
                                legend.key.size = unit(0.4,"cm"), legend.text=element_text(size=9),
                                legend.title=element_text(size=10))
```

```{r Fig 2 repeated testing by stunting ABSOLUTE}
##perform repeated spearman by country within sample type. (combat-adjusted data.) - for ABSOLUTE ABUNDANCES
Xabs       = data_bile %>% dplyr::select( all_of(c(acids_abund_col, meta_cols ) )) %>%
  group_by(SampleType) %>%
  filter(!duplicated(id)) %>% #for most downstream analyses, remove the technical duplicates
  ungroup()

Dabs <- Xabs %>% filter(SampleType=="Duodenal")
Gabs <- Xabs %>% filter(SampleType=="Gastric")

df_feces_abs <- Fabs %>% select(all_of(c(acids_abund_col))) %>% select(-any_of(rareF_abs)) #pick the right BAs
dim(df_feces_abs) #78 bile acids left, hm.
identical(df_feces_abs$allocholic_acid3sul, Fabs$allocholic_acid3sul) #confirm order ok
```

## Figure 2F
```{r}
##for reviewer 3: plot the absolute abundance data as ratios, LCA/CDCA, and DCA/CA
#Define ratios, absolute
head(Fabs) #the absolute data, fecal, including metadata.
summary(Fabs$chenodeoxycholic_acid) #there are some zeros
summary(Fabs$cholic_acid) #there are some zeros 
Fabs$LCA_CDCA_ratio <- Fabs$lithocholic_acid / (Fabs$chenodeoxycholic_acid)
Fabs$LCA_CDCA_ratio <- ifelse(Fabs$LCA_CDCA_ratio==Inf, yes = Fabs$lithocholic_acid/(Fabs$chenodeoxycholic_acid + min(Fabs$chenodeoxycholic_acid[which(Fabs$chenodeoxycholic_acid!=0)])/2), no=Fabs$LCA_CDCA_ratio) #instead of zero, impute as half minimum
Fabs$DCA_CA_ratio <- Fabs$deoxycholic_acid / Fabs$cholic_acid
Fabs$DCA_CA_ratio <- ifelse(Fabs$DCA_CA_ratio==Inf, yes = Fabs$deoxycholic_acid/(Fabs$cholic_acid + min(Fabs$cholic_acid[which(Fabs$cholic_acid!=0)])/2), no=Fabs$DCA_CA_ratio)


#plot and test ratios by stunting status
Fabs$stunted <- factor(Fabs$stunted, levels=c("non-stunted", "stunted"))
fig2F <- ggplot(Fabs, aes(x=stunted, y=log(LCA_CDCA_ratio))) + geom_boxplot(outlier.shape=NA) + 
  geom_jitter(width=0.1, height=0) +
  theme(panel.background = element_blank(), axis.line = element_line(colour = "black"),
               axis.title.y = element_text(margin = margin(r = 10))) +
  xlab("Stunting") + ylab("LCA:CDCA Log Ratio") + ggtitle("LCA:CDCA Conversion") + 
  annotate('segment', x=1, xend=2, y=10, yend=10) + annotate('text', label=("***"), x=1.5, y=11)

pdf("../../Figure_panels/Figure2F.pdf", height = 4, width = 4)
fig2F
dev.off()

source_data_2F <- Fabs %>% select(stunted, LCA_CDCA_ratio)

write.csv2(source_data_2F, "../../Source_data/Figure2F.csv")

#test significance.
wilcox.test(Fabs$LCA_CDCA_ratio~Fabs$stunted) #p=5.7e-05 #hurrah!
wilcox_effsize(Fabs, LCA_CDCA_ratio ~ stunted, ci = TRUE) #
```

## Figure 2E
```{r Fig 2E stunting heatmap REVISED}
##REVISED version of this heatmap: as per reviewer 3 concerned about ComBat: pick the bile acids based on non-ComBat-corrected nonparametric test results, and star based on LM

#first: summarize the mean value of each bile acid per stunting status.
#since this is a stunting heatmap, take stunting hits only, not HAZ
stunting_all <- full_join(diff_stunting, diff_stunting2)
diff_stunt_sig <- stunting_all %>% filter(Test%in%c("Wilcoxon","Wilcoxon_combat")&qval<0.05&Outcome=="Stunted")
to_summarize <- feces %>% dplyr::select(all_of(c(diff_stunt_sig$Bile_Acid, 'stunted'))) #take the hits only #from raw data (?) 
to_summarize[is.na(to_summarize)] <- 0 #0 is 0, no NAs
AverageByStunt <- to_summarize %>% dplyr::group_by(stunted) %>% 
  dplyr::summarize_all(mean, na.rm=TRUE) #take 3 categories to visualize
AverageByStunt #nice :) 
AverageByStunt <- AverageByStunt %>% pivot_longer(cols=c(2:length(names(AverageByStunt))),
                                                            names_to="Bile_Acid", values_to="Relative_Abundance")
AverageByStunt #double nice :) 
AverageByStunt <- AverageByStunt[order(AverageByStunt$Relative_Abundance),]

pdata <- AverageByStunt 
mylevels <- pdata %>% filter(stunted=='stunted')
pdata$Bile_Acid <- factor(pdata$Bile_Acid, levels=mylevels$Bile_Acid)

#sig hits #filter now for must be sig WITH and WITHOUT Combat
with_combat <- diff_stunt_sig %>% filter(Test=='Wilcoxon_combat'&qval<0.05)
without_combat <- diff_stunt_sig %>% filter(Test=='Wilcoxon'&qval<0.05)
pdata <- pdata %>% filter(Bile_Acid %in% c(with_combat$Bile_Acid) & Bile_Acid %in% c(without_combat$Bile_Acid))

#scale everything rowwise relative to the average abundance of the bile acid
pdata2 <- pdata %>% group_by(Bile_Acid) %>% mutate(Abund_Avg=mean(Relative_Abundance, na.omit=TRUE))
pdata2$Scaled_Abund <- pdata2$Relative_Abundance / pdata2$Abund_Avg
##add a star in case it is also raw significant in the LMs #with covariates? Sure?
lm_stars <- diff_stunting %>% filter(SampleType=="Feces"&pval<0.05&Test=="LM_cov") #should we specify, either stunting or HAZ as outcome? or keep both?
pdata2$lm_sig <- ifelse(pdata2$stunted=='stunted' & #only put the star for one tile
                          pdata2$Bile_Acid %in% lm_stars$Bile_Acid, "*", "")

figure_2E <- ggplot(pdata2, aes(x=stunted, y=Bile_Acid, fill=Scaled_Abund,label=lm_sig)) + geom_tile(colour='black') +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust=1)) + 
  geom_text(colour='white', size=6) +
  xlab(NULL) + 
  ylab(NULL) + 
  scale_fill_viridis() + 
  labs(fill="Log Rel. Abund.") + ggtitle("Fecal Bile Acids Differentially Abundant by Stunting") +
  coord_flip()

pdf("../../Figure_panels/Figure2E.pdf", height = 3, width = 4.5)
figure_2E
dev.off()

write.csv2(pdata2, "../../Source_data/Figure2E.csv")

#also add a panel for primary vs. secondary bile acids as per Fig 1.
#bile acids defined above.

#one row per bile acid actually shown in the heatmap, in the same order as the heatmap y-axis
sidebar_data <- pdata2 %>% dplyr::distinct(Bile_Acid)
sidebar_data$Class <- bile_acid_class[as.character(sidebar_data$Bile_Acid)]
sidebar_data$Class[is.na(sidebar_data$Class)] <- "Unclassified" #safety net if a new bile acid ever shows up
table(sidebar_data$Class, useNA="ifany") #check nothing fell through as Unclassified

p_sidebar <- ggplot(sidebar_data, aes(y=1, x=Bile_Acid, fill=Class)) + geom_tile(colour='black')
p_sidebar <- p_sidebar + scale_fill_manual(values=c(Primary="black", Secondary="grey80", Group="white", Unclassified="red"), drop=FALSE)
p_sidebar <- p_sidebar + theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), axis.text.y = element_blank(),
                                axis.ticks = element_blank(), panel.background = element_blank(),
                                legend.key.size = unit(0.4,"cm"), legend.text=element_text(size=9),
                                legend.title=element_text(size=10))
p_sidebar <- p_sidebar + xlab(NULL) + ylab(NULL) + labs(fill="Bile Acid Type")

p_combined <- ggarrange(p_sidebar, p, nrow=2, align="hv", heights=c(0.4, 0.45))

#pdf(width=6, height=5, "/Users/khuus/ownCloud/KH-PhD/BileAcidsManuscript/Revisions_08.2026/plots/2E_Heatmap_BileAcidsbySTUNT_wsidebar_revised2.pdf")
print(p_combined)
#dev.off()
```

```{r compare rel and abs AAT}
#OK how about this: we simply join the tables.
diff_aat_rel_join <- diff_aat %>% dplyr::rename(pval_rel=pval, qval_rel=qval, coef_rel=coef)
diff_aat_abs_join <- diff_aat_abs %>% dplyr::rename(pval_abs=pval, qval_abs=qval,
                                                  coef_abs=coef)
#remove the 'rel abund' flag of all bile acids in the rel abund datA
diff_aat_rel_join$Bile_Acid <- gsub("_r", "", diff_aat_rel_join$Bile_Acid)

#the two chunks label the same test differently 
diff_aat_abs_join$Test <- gsub("_ABS$", "", diff_aat_abs_join$Test, ignore.case=TRUE)
diff_aat_rel_join$Test     <- gsub("_combat$", "", diff_aat_rel_join$Test, ignore.case=TRUE)

diff_aat_compare <- full_join(diff_aat_rel_join, diff_aat_abs_join)
View(diff_aat_compare) #there it is, finally.
diff_aat_compare$qboth <- ifelse(diff_aat_compare$qval_rel<0.05&diff_aat_compare$qval_abs<0.05, "yes", "no")
diff_aat_compare$pboth <- ifelse(diff_aat_compare$pval_rel<0.05&diff_aat_compare$pval_abs<0.05, "yes", "no")

#write.csv(diff_aat_compare, "/Users/khuus/ownCloud/KH-PhD/BileAcidsManuscript/Revisions_08.2026/aat_results_abs_vs_rel_compare.csv")

#test a few little dplyr statistics for the reviewers
diff_aat_compare_sig <- diff_aat_compare %>% filter(qval_rel<0.05) #compare based on hits
dim(diff_aat_compare_sig) #46 original hits
dplyr::count(diff_aat_compare_sig, pboth) %>% mutate(per=n/sum(n)*100) #45, 80.3%
dplyr::count(diff_aat_compare_sig, qboth) %>% mutate(per=n/sum(n)*100) #40, 71.4%
```

```{r Fig 3F AAT heatmap REVISED}
#as per previous heatmaps, revised to use the nonparametric data first.
##REVISED version of this heatmap: as per reviewer 3 concerned about ComBat: pick the bile acids based on non-ComBat-corrected nonparametric test results, and star based on LM
diff_aat_sig2 <- p.res.aat.f.noc %>% filter(qval<0.05) %>% #feces hits, no combat, sig.
  full_join(p.res.aat.f) %>% filter(qval<0.05) #but also the combat hits

to_summarize <- feces %>% dplyr::select(all_of(c(diff_aat_sig2$Bile_Acid, 'aat'))) 

to_summarize <- feces %>% dplyr::select(all_of(c(ba_cols, "aat")))
to_summarize[is.na(to_summarize)] <- 0 #0 is 0, no NAs
AverageByAAT <- to_summarize %>% dplyr::group_by(aat) %>%
  dplyr::summarize_all(mean, na.rm=TRUE) #take 3 categories to visualize
AverageByAAT #nice :) 
AverageByAAT <- AverageByAAT %>% pivot_longer(cols=c(2:length(names(AverageByAAT))),
                                                            names_to="Bile_Acid", values_to="Relative_Abundance")
AverageByAAT #double nice :) 
AverageByAAT <- AverageByAAT[order(AverageByAAT$Relative_Abundance),]

pdata <- AverageByAAT
mylevels <- pdata %>% filter(aat=="elevated")
pdata$Bile_Acid <- factor(pdata$Bile_Acid, levels=mylevels$Bile_Acid)

#sig hits #and no missing AAT data
combat_hits <- p.res.aat.f %>% filter(Test=="Spearman_combat"&qval<0.05)
noncombat_hits <- p.res.aat.f.noc %>% filter(Test=="Spearman"&qval<0.05)
pdata <- pdata %>% filter(Bile_Acid %in% c(combat_hits$Bile_Acid) & 
                            Bile_Acid %in% c(noncombat_hits$Bile_Acid) &
                            aat %in% c("normal", "elevated"))

#scale everything rowwise relative to the average abundance of the bile acid
pdata2 <- pdata %>% group_by(Bile_Acid) %>% mutate(Abund_Avg=mean(Relative_Abundance, na.omit=TRUE))
pdata2$Scaled_Abund <- pdata2$Relative_Abundance / pdata2$Abund_Avg
#add a star in case it is also raw significant in the LMs
lm_stars <- diff_aat %>% filter(SampleType=="Feces"&pval<0.05&Test=="LM_cov")
pdata2$lm_sig <- ifelse(pdata2$aat=="elevated" & #only put the star for one tile
                          pdata2$Bile_Acid %in% lm_stars$Bile_Acid, "*", "")

Figure3F <- ggplot(pdata2, aes(x=aat, y=Bile_Acid, fill=Scaled_Abund,label=lm_sig)) + 
  geom_tile(colour='black') +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust=1)) + 
  geom_text(colour='white') +
  xlab(NULL) + 
  ylab(NULL) + 
  scale_fill_viridis() + 
  labs(fill="Log Rel. Abund.") + ggtitle("Fecal Bile Acids Differentially Abundant by AAT") +
  coord_flip()

pdf("../../Figure_panels/Figure3F.pdf",width=6.5, height=3.5)
Figure3F
dev.off()

write.csv2(pdata2, "../../Source_data/Figure3F.csv")

#also add a panel for primary vs. secondary bile acids as per Fig 1.
#bile acids defined above.

#one row per bile acid actually shown in the heatmap, in the same order as the heatmap y-axis
sidebar_data <- pdata2 %>% dplyr::distinct(Bile_Acid)
sidebar_data$Class <- bile_acid_class[as.character(sidebar_data$Bile_Acid)]
sidebar_data$Class[is.na(sidebar_data$Class)] <- "Unclassified" #safety net if a new bile acid ever shows up
table(sidebar_data$Class, useNA="ifany") #check nothing fell through as Unclassified

p_sidebar <- ggplot(sidebar_data, aes(y=1, x=Bile_Acid, fill=Class)) + geom_tile(colour='black')
p_sidebar <- p_sidebar + scale_fill_manual(values=c(Primary="black", Secondary="grey80", Group="white", Unclassified="red"), drop=FALSE)
p_sidebar <- p_sidebar + theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(), axis.text.y = element_blank(),
                                axis.ticks = element_blank(), panel.background = element_blank(),
                                legend.key.size = unit(0.4,"cm"), legend.text=element_text(size=9),
                                legend.title=element_text(size=10))
p_sidebar <- p_sidebar + xlab(NULL) + ylab(NULL) + labs(fill="Bile Acid Type")

p_combined <- ggarrange(p_sidebar, p, nrow=2, align="hv", heights=c(0.45, 0.5))

print(p_combined)
```
